english.title: Keeper of animals moved off holding fail to complete/provide movement document (Wales)
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a keeper of animals of the ovine or caprine species, namely **(..SPECIFY ANIMALS..), failed, when moving an animal off your holding at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), to

(A)_[complete a movement document in accordance with Section C of the Annex to the Council Regulation and in a form approved by the Welsh Ministers in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)]_
(B)_[provide the transporter of the animal with a copy of a movement document completed in accordance with Section C of the Annex to the Council Regulation and in a form approved by the Welsh Ministers]_
english.legislation: Contrary to article 24(7) of the Sheep and Goats (Records, Identification and Movement) (Wales) Order 2015 and sections 73 and 75 Animal Health Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section C of the Annex to the Council Regulation (EC) No 21/2004 contains the requirements of the movement document.
(ii) The requirements in Article 24(7) are subject to subsections (8), (9) and (10) which provide for situations in which the procedure in (7) may be deviated from. Please see Article 24 for full information.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale. Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
